issues.where: the constituent element of sovereignty follows the well-born one
issues.problem: aiśvarya is not one of the prakṛtis, and a singular 'constituent element of sovereignty' has no referent in the system; here prakṛti is used in its ordinary sense 'nature' (svabhāva): 'sovereignty by its nature attaches to the well-born'. The glossary rendering applies to prakṛti = the seven constituents, not to this sense. The Hindi 'ऐश्वर्य की प्रकृति' is fine, since प्रकृति also means nature.
issues.fix: The constituent elements of their own accord submit to a weak king of high birth; sovereignty by its nature follows the well-born one.

patch.old: the constituent element of sovereignty follows the well-born one
patch.new: sovereignty by its nature follows the well-born one

issues.problem: Same: gloss as 'the nature of sovereignty'.
Note should record the alternative the other way round (nature chosen, constituents as alternative).

patch.value: aiśvarya-prakṛti taken as 'the nature (svabhāva) of sovereignty', i.e. sovereignty by its nature attaches to high birth; the alternative 'the constituents (subjects) of the realm' is possible but aiśvarya is not one of the seven prakṛtis. Hindi प्रकृति covers both senses.

issues.where: destruction of the standing crop is worse than destruction of the handful (the reaped grain)
issues.problem: 'standing' and '(the reaped grain)' put one contested interpretation of muṣṭi into the translation. The causal reading of prayāsa-vadhāt is right (parallel to nirājīvatvāt), but the 'loss of effort' argument fits muṣṭi = the handful of seed sown (little effort lost) at least as well as reaped grain. Keep the translation literal and leave the interpretation in notes.
issues.fix: Because it destroys the effort (spent on it), destruction of the crop is worse than destruction of the handful; because it leaves no livelihood, drought is worse than excessive rain.

Splits, sandhi and grammar labels checked against the Sanskrit for every unit: all correct, including 19 (pāpa-rogī + apāpa-rogī, no text_flag needed), 13 (-mūla bahuvrīhis), 3 (simile reading, medium confidence honest), 21 (genitive kept literal), 25 (causal ablative parallel to nirājīvatvāt). No regrouping suggested.
